classification.difficultyReason: Requires solving a cubic product inequality after multiplying by the denominator squared, retaining an equality endpoint and excluding both original poles.

answer.short:
$\dfrac13\leq x<1$ or $x>3$.

Multiply by the denominator squared, solve $(3x-1)(x-1)(x-3)\geq0$, and exclude $x=1,3$.
answer.worked:
The original denominator is $(x-1)(x-3)$, so $x\ne1,3$. Multiply by $(x^2-4x+3)^2$, which is positive on this domain.

$$\begin{align*}(x^2-x+2)(x^2-4x+3)&\geq(x^2-4x+3)^2\\(x^2-x+2)(x^2-4x+3)-(x^2-4x+3)^2&\geq0\\{}[(x^2-x+2)-(x^2-4x+3)](x^2-4x+3)&\geq0\\(3x-1)(x-1)(x-3)&\geq0\end{align*}$$

The critical values are $\frac13,1,3$. The product has signs $-,+,-,+$ on the four successive intervals.

Include $x=\frac13$, but exclude the original denominator zeroes $x=1,3$. Hence $\boxed{\frac13\leq x<1\text{ or }x>3}$.
